data.name: Kleophan
data.long_meaning: The name Kleophan is derived from the Greek word κλεοπάτηρ (kleopatēr), which means 'glory of God'. In the Christian tradition, the name Kleophan is associated with several saints, including St. Cleophas, the brother of St. Joseph and uncle of Jesus, and St. Cleophas of Rome, a martyr under Emperor Diocletian.
data.spiritual_meaning: Reflecting the glory of God in one's actions and character

in_hebrew.name: קליאופאן
in_hebrew.long_meaning: קליאופאן הוא שם פרטי שמקורו ביוונית ומשמעותו 'אלוהים מואיל להראות פניו' או 'אלוהים מראה פניו'. השם נגזר מהמילים היווניות 'κλέος' (כבוד) ו'φάνε' (להראות). בקונטקסט הנוצרי, השם מייצג את הרעיון של אלוהים המתגלה לבני האדם ומעניק להם כבוד והדרכה.

in_greek.name: Κλεοφάν
in_greek.meaning: Ο Θεός δείχνει το πρόσωπό Του
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Κλεοφάν προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις 'κλέος' (δόξα) και 'φάνε' (να δείχνω). Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, το όνομα αυτό συμβολίζει την έκφραση της θείας παρουσίας και της δόξας του Θεού. Οι πρώτοι Χριστιανοί χρησιμοποιούσαν το όνομα για να εκφράσουν την πίστη τους στην αποκάλυψη του Θεού μέσω του Ιησού Χριστού.

in_latin.name: Cleophan
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Cleophan derivatur ex vocibus Graecis 'κλέος' (gloria) et 'φάνε' (ostendere). In traditione christiana, nomen hoc significat revelationem Dei et manifestationem gloriae eius. Quod nomen olim a primis Christianis adhibebatur ad exprimendam fidem in Deum, qui se revelavit per Jesum Christum.

in_english.name: Kleophan
in_english.meaning: Glorious manifestation of God, God shows His face
in_english.long_meaning: The name Kleophan originates from Greek roots 'κλέος' (glory) and 'φάνε' (to show). It signifies the glorious manifestation of God or God's revelation of His face to humanity. In Christian tradition, Kleophan represents the concept of divine disclosure and the glory of God made manifest through Jesus Christ. Historically, the name has been associated with spiritual illumination and guidance. Today, Kleophan is used across various Christian cultures to symbolize a deep connection with the divine.

historical_references.reference: Kleophas, a disciple of Saint Peter, is mentioned in the New Testament (Matthew 27:56, Mark 15:40, and Luke 24:51). He is listed among the Galilean followers of Jesus who were present at the crucifixion, the burial, and the resurrection.

Kleophas, also known as Cleophas or Alpheus, is mentioned in the Gospel of John (19:25) as the father of James the Less, one of the brothers of Jesus. This reference is less certain as it does not appear in the Synoptic Gospels.
